lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The controlling holder proposed on 2026-11-06 to take XYF private at $6.03/ADS cash, a 28.3% premium to the prior close. The bidder holds ~94% of votes and ~48% of shares (13D: 110.9m shares, 47.97% of class, with Class B at 20 votes). A special committee of three independent directors was formed on 2026-11-18. Spot $5.23 is 15.3% below the bid, so the stock trades as a wide-spread arb. The only in-window paths to a big move are a deal update with the release (definitive agreement: low probability, ~5%, roughly +12%) or a hint the bid is being cut or withdrawn (~2%, roughly -10%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The proposal day itself moved +22.34% (11-06). The two later deal filings (AGM notice 11-16, special committee 11-19) moved -1.11% and -0.19% per baseline.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 loan volume is likely to shrink again from Q2's RMB11.63bn. Q2 was -20.5% QoQ and -70.2% YoY, and the company withdrew guidance. A 2026-09-27 industry piece says Chinese loan-facilitation platforms were broadly contracting under the new fee/APR rules, including a 2026 rule folding fees into an annualised cost (one of seven listed platforms growing). So revenue, near RMB994m in Q2, likely falls again QoQ. The shrink is the expected base case, with no guide to miss, and the deal anchor damps it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume/guide disappointments drove -15.7% (Q3'25) and -26.2% (Q4'25, weak Q1 guide) before the proposal. The Q2'26 volume at the low end of the guide got +2.04%.

findings.finding: Credit improved in Q2: 31-60 day delinquency fell to 1.73% from 2.61% in Q1, and 91-180 day to 9.09% from 9.95%. The loan-receivable provision fell to ~RMB10.1m from ~RMB52.3m in Q1, and net income rose 23.8% QoQ to RMB47.0m. If the release continues, Q3 profit can rise QoQ even on lower volume, and a richer profit print makes the $6.03 (~0.2x Q2 book equity of RMB7.76bn, ~$1.14bn) look safer or bumpable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's provision-driven profit uptick with the low-end volume print got +2.04%.

findings.finding: Since the 11-06 proposal the stock has slid from $5.75 to $5.23 (-9%), widening the spread to the $6.03 bid from 4.9% to 15.3%. That is not explained by any filing: the only later 6-Ks are the AGM notice (no proposals) and the special committee. The market prices material doubt or a long timeline. A routine release that confirms the process is under way, without signalling a price cut, can narrow that slightly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print under a pending bid.

findings.finding: The next guide is likely absent or cautious. Management withdrew quantitative guidance at Q2 and the bidder is the CEO's affiliate, so the outlook commentary is controlled by the buyer. A gloomy outlook (regulatory language already warns past profitability should not be assumed) supports the bidder's price and can widen the spread.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4'25 print with a weak Q1 guide fell 26.19%. The Q2'26 print that withdrew guidance rose 2.04%.

findings.finding: The $100m buyback expires on 2026-11-30 with ~$35.5m unused as of 08-14. The semi-annual $0.28/ADS dividend is declared with Q2 and Q4 results, not Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Dividends were declared with the Q4'25 (-26.19%) and Q2'26 (+2.04%) prints; no measurable reaction to capital return on its own.

findings.finding: Qfin, the largest US-listed peer in the same China consumer-credit facilitation channel, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-24 after FINV last spoke. It beat a lowered bar, with non-GAAP net income of RMB416.5m against a guide of 400-500m. It then guided Q4 net income to RMB210-310m (non-GAAP 250-350m, down 67-77% year on year), reported a 90+ day delinquency of 2.50%, day-1 delinquency of 5.8% and loan volume down 40.6% year on year, and the CEO cited 'clear erosion in risk performance', an 'industry-wide liquidity squeeze' and regulation persisting into 2027. QFIN fell 11.2% on 2026-11-25. The read-through is that FINV's Q4 and FY commentary is likely to show the same deterioration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FINV fell 15.4% after Q2 2026 on the 'lower part' FY guide and the warned Q3 China contraction (2026-08-28). QFIN's Q3 2025 print slid 13% after hours, as did FINV's Q3 2025 (-13.9% on 2025-11-20).

findings.finding: FINV's FY2026 revenue guide is RMB11.5-12.9bn, at the 'lower part'. The street's average is already below the low end at RMB11.31bn (range 10.9-11.6bn; EPS RMB5.32, down 47.6%). The H2 revenue the street implies (about 4.70bn against H1 of 6.61bn) means a formal cut to about 11.0-11.5bn would match expectations. Only a cut below about RMB10.9bn, or a Q4 profit outlook as steep as Qfin's, is new negative information.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance moved the stock at the last two prints: -15.4% on 2026-08-28 on the 'lower part' language, and +10.2% on 2026-05-26 with a reaffirmed guide plus a new $150m buyback.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-08-27) FINV said China volume was 'down around 50% in July', early risk indicators were 'up around 20% versus the second quarter', funding cost rose 30bp to 3.7% with 'further upward pressure' expected, and the collection crackdown hurt recovery efficiency. Q3 provisions and margin should therefore be weaker than Q2, which had net profit of RMB426.8m. The company has already told the market this, so the item sits inside guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The reported quarter has mattered less than the guide: Q2 2026 net profit down 43% was absorbed into a guide-driven -15.4%.

findings.finding: FINV trades below its cash. Cash plus short-term investments were RMB6.42bn (US$946m) at 2026-06-30, and management cited RMB7.5bn of cash plus about RMB5bn of highly liquid assets on the call. The company has a $150m buyback authorised from 2026-05-30 to 2028-05-29 and bought $66.8m in H1. The Q3 release normally discloses the buyback amount, and any acceleration or new return at this valuation is a long-side catalyst.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print, announced with the new $150m buyback, rose 10.2% (2026-05-26; Simply Wall St notes about +15% after the news).

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A depressed setup has not protected this name: Q3 2025 (-13.9%) and Q2 2026 (-15.4%) both fell further.

findings.finding: Indonesia's OJK P2P lending data for September 2026 shows the industry's 90+ day default rate (TWP90) at 5.36%, up from 4.73% in August and above OJK's 5% threshold, with outstanding-loan growth slowing to 17.0% year on year from 22.1%. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The overseas segment has been the positive offset in recent prints (Q2 overseas operating profit more than doubled); no reaction to an overseas miss is on record.

findings.finding: Chinese banks are cutting their online-platform partnerships. Jilin Yillion Bank went from 56 customer-acquisition partners in November 2024 to 10 in July 2026. Online-marketing measures for financial products took effect on 30 September, and regulators told e-commerce apps on 21 September to stop selling loans. Funding and traffic stay tight into Q4. China Daily also expects leading platforms to gain share as smaller ones exit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Regulatory tightening drove the 2026 de-rating across the group; FINV's guide-driven -15.4% in August cited funding tightening.

findings.finding: FINV is the relative survivor of its group. In H1 2026 revenue fell about 6% and profit about 43%, against Qfin's revenue -25%, Jiayin's first interim loss (Q2 volume RMB9.5bn), X Financial's Q2 volume -70% and Vcredit's -84%. Lexin guided a possible Q3 net loss. Peers trade at $0.25 (YRD, with an NYSE price notice) to $1.17 (JFIN). If competitors exit, leading platforms can take share and acquisition costs fall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of FINV being rewarded for relative resilience; it has traded with the group.
